faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Whether you're a guest or a venue owner, the answer to your question is probably here.
faq.g1q: Can I use tokens I bought at one venue at another venue?
faq.g1a: Yes. Your token balance is kept in a single wallet and is valid at every venue that uses PlayMyJam. You can spend the rest of the tokens you bought at one venue at another.
faq.g2q: Do I need to download an app or sign up?
faq.g2a: No. Scanning the QR code on the table opens the venue's page in your browser. You don't need an account to browse songs; if you want to use your tokens across devices and venues, you can link an account in a few seconds.
faq.g3q: What if the song I want isn't on the list?
faq.g3a: You can send a song you can't find as a request to the venue. If the venue approves it, the song becomes available to add for a short time and you're notified.
faq.g4a: You see the estimated wait before adding your song, and after adding it you follow the queue live on your phone. The priority queue goes ahead of songs in the normal queue.
faq.g5q: Can I request the same song again?
faq.g5a: A song can't be added while it's playing or already in the queue. It can be requested again 30 minutes after it started playing, so the same song doesn't play back to back.
faq.g6q: What happens to my tokens if my song doesn't play?
faq.g6a: If the venue rejects your song request, the tokens you spent are automatically returned to your balance.
faq.g7q: Is payment secure, and can I get a refund?
faq.g7a: Payments are taken by credit or debit card over a 256-bit SSL encrypted connection. Your card details are not stored by us; transactions are processed through a licensed payment institution's infrastructure. If you haven't used any of the tokens you bought, you can request a refund within 14 days of the purchase date. Details are on the Delivery and Refund Terms page.
faq.v1q: Will putting PlayMyJam in my venue cause copyright problems?
faq.v1a: PlayMyJam does not host any audio or video files and does not sell you a music licence; it is software that queues guests' requests. The permits needed to play music in a business (from collecting societies such as MESAM, MSG and MÜYAP) are already an obligation of every business that plays music; PlayMyJam adds no new obligation. The details are written in your contract.
faq.v2q: What do I need to get set up, and does it cost anything?
faq.v2a: Setup is free. Your existing screen or speaker setup and a browser are enough; no extra device is needed. We prepare the QR codes for your tables.
faq.v3q: Do I stay in control of the music?
faq.v3a: Yes, you always have the final say. Guests only choose from your lists; songs that aren't on them never play without your approval. From the dashboard you can skip songs, reorder the queue, set the volume and temporarily close guest additions during busy hours.
faq.v4q: Can I use my own playlists?
faq.v4a: Yes. You can import your existing playlists into the dashboard or build new ones from the catalog. When there are no requests, music continues from these lists automatically, so your venue is never silent.
faq.v5a: You receive a revenue share from the paid tokens guests spend on songs. Rates and payment periods are written in your contract, and you track your earnings from the dashboard.
faq.v6a: Just fill in the Register Your Venue form; our team will call you and guide you through the contract and setup.

about.title: Guests choose the venue's music.
about.p1: PlayMyJam is a song-request platform that lets guests decide the music playing in cafes, bars and restaurants. Guests scan the QR code on the table, pick a song from the venue's catalog and add it to the queue with a token, then follow live on their phone when it will play.
about.p2: Our mission is to let people take an active part in the atmosphere of the place they're in, and to give venues a modern tool that connects them with their guests and brings in extra revenue. The venue runs the music from a single dashboard and decides at any moment which playlists play, which requests are accepted and how loud it is.
about.copyrightTitle: No need to worry about copyright.
about.copyrightLead: This isn't just a claim; it's written into our contract with venues.
about.c1Title: We don't host any music files.
about.c2Title: Music licensing is the venue's responsibility.
about.c3Title: A token is not a licence fee.

blocked.title: Notifications are blocked on this device
blocked.intro: Browser rules stop us from asking again here; you need to allow it once in your device settings. Come back to this screen afterwards — we'll take care of the rest.
blocked.androidApp: Phone Settings → Apps → find this app (it appears under the venue's name) → Notifications → allow.
blocked.androidBrowser: In Chrome, tap the lock icon in the address bar → Permissions (or Site settings) → Notifications → Reset.
blocked.ios: Phone Settings → Notifications → pick this app from the list → Allow Notifications.
blocked.desktop: Click the lock icon in the address bar → Notifications → Allow, then reload the page.
blocked.stillBlocked: Permission still looks off. Make sure the setting is saved and try again.
blocked.recovered: Notifications are on — you're all set.
